subject: Short-notice hotfix: inference integrity patch — immediate actions
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Akira Tanaka <akira@datasynth.co>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-notice hotfix: inference integrity patch — immediate actions

Hi Akira,

Quick note from ops: we identified a rare KV-cache state corruption that, under certain warmup patterns, can cause token duplication and elevated latency on a small set of model variants serving the prefix-heavy workloads. The issue affects ~0.6% of requests across a narrow shard set and was first detected at 08:45 PT.

We plan a short, unscheduled hotfix to correct the cache compaction logic and reconcile affected KV entries. The deploy is small but intrusive — expected window is ~8–15 minutes for the shard set, with rolling updates across replicas. We aim to run the patch starting at 09:40 PT (in ~25 minutes) unless you ask us to delay.

What we need from you (if applicable):
- Pause any large batch job or scheduled inference runs between 09:30–10:00 PT if you can.
- If you have in-flight critical requests, reply and we will prioritize excluding those keys from reconciliation.

Attachments: hotfix_patch_notes_v1.pdf (summary), trace-snippet-20281103.log (sample traces).

Apologies for the short notice — we prefer to correct this now to avoid regression in prompt-sensitive paths. Please reply to acknowledge and tell us if you need us to delay.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Short-notice hotfix: inference integrity patch — immediate actions

Stephanie / Akira — technical update from infra: 

Root cause (brief): a race in prefix compaction allowed stale KV pointers to persist when concurrent warmup requests interleaved with background compaction. That leads to mismatched KV reads and, in rare cases, repeated tokens and occasional increased latency while the runtime retries.

Mitigation plan (what the hotfix does):
- Reconcile and invalidate stale KV pointers for affected shard set.
- Harden compaction path (small code change with no model weights changes).
- Add a short-lived feature-flag that forces older replicas to drain cache before accepting traffic to avoid reintroducing stale state.

Impact estimate: 6–12 minutes per shard set; we will roll shards sequentially to keep regional availability. During the reconcile we may return transient 503s for a tiny percentage of requests; no permanent model behavior changes expected (model weights and generation algorithms unchanged).

Rollback plan: we will stop the reconcile and toggle the feature-flag off. We have a snapshot of KV state taken at 09:05 PT; rollback will restore that snapshot to the small shard set (expected <10 minutes). Full text runbook attached: rollback_plan.txt.

Monitoring & verification: we will stream sampled responses to a verification job and watch for token-dup metrics and latency percentiles; I will stay on the incident channel during the window.

Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Akira — quick follow-up with schedule and links.

We will begin the rolling hotfix at 09:40 PT, starting with us-west-2 primary shards (you asked us to prioritize us-west). Expected completion for your region by 09:52 PT. If anything changes we'll post updates to the incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4371

Please pause any large jobs that could be affected between 09:30–10:00 PT. We'll send a short post-deploy verification checklist (3–4 quick checks your team can run) and sample responses to confirm token integrity.

If you absolutely cannot accept any transient 5xx/duplication during the window we can delay, but we recommend the short fix now to prevent wider exposure tonight.

Thanks for the quick reply — I'll keep you updated as we start.

-Stephanie
